hints: Salary updates change one employee's current salary; range queries count salaries in an inclusive interval.
Compress all salary values that can appear, including update replacements and query boundaries if useful.
A Fenwick tree stores how many employees currently have each compressed salary.
analogy: Keep a frequency counter over ordered salary coordinates; updates move one count and queries sum a coordinate range.
example: If salaries 30,50,50 and query [40,60], the frequency sum is 2.
algorithm: Read operations offline to collect salaries, coordinate-compress them, initialize Fenwick frequencies. For update, remove old salary count and add new; for query [a,b], subtract prefix(<a) from prefix(<=b).
correctness: The Fenwick prefix sum equals the number of employees up to that salary coordinate; subtracting two prefixes isolates the requested interval.
complexity: O((n+q) log(n+q)) time and O(n+q) space.
